title: UK PPI — October 2026 producer price inflation (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the same-minute twin of the October CPI print
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/producerpriceinflationukoctober2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 39,976 bytes) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Producer price inflation, UK: October 2026', 'Release date: 18 November 2026 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published'. Cadence independently reproduced from the publisher's own previous-releases listing, fetched the same day: October 2024 data released 20 Nov 2024, October 2025 data released 19 Nov 2025 — the October reference month lands on the third Wednesday of November every year. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-cpi-2026-11-18, 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/uk-ppi-2026-11-18.from-uk-cpi-2026-11-18.json (read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). THE PROPOSAL'S PLACEMENT FINDING SURVIVES AND ITS MECHANISM DOES NOT. Placement: this is the only tracked release publishing in the SAME 07:00 London minute as a UK CPI print, so any 02:00 ET UK reaction on 11-18 has two candidate causes. Verified today to be STRUCTURAL, not a one-off — four ONS release pages fetched direct give PPI at 07:00 on 2026-09-16, 2026-10-21, 2026-11-18 and 2026-12-16, each matching a tracked or proposed UK CPI date exactly. Mechanism REFUTED: the proposal said PPI input prices see 'the wholesale and cap moves WITHOUT the consumer VAT cut'. PPI sees NEITHER tax. ONS's PPI QMI (fetched 2026-09-09, last revised 22 Oct 2025) states 'All index numbers exclude Value Added Tax (VAT)', so SI 2026/987 is invisible here by measurement rule; and the PPI Fuel group (2.5% of the input basket) is priced from a DESNZ panel covering 'the supply of gas and electricity to industrial and commercial end-users', data ONS says 'differ from the data provided for the purposes of the Consumer Prices Index', while Ofgem's own page states 'You are not protected by the price cap if you... have a business energy contract'. Wholesale yes; cap no; VAT never. WHAT THE PRINT ACTUALLY IS: a lagged restatement of Brent in sterling. The QMI states businesses report 'transactions that occur on or near to the first of each month', so the October index is a 1-October snapshot published 48 days later, and crude (weight 6.9%) explained ~73-76% of the input index's monthly move in both June and July 2026. Base case, against the published disinflation narrative (input 7.4% -> 4.9%): input annual rate 6.5-8.0% in the October print, output 3.3-3.9%, because first-week Brent in GBP ran +12.0% in August and +16.3% MTD in September against a flat Oct-2025 base. DATA-QUALITY FLAG: PPI is designated 'official statistics', NOT accredited, is under an OSR Spotlight-on-Quality improvement plan awaiting reaccreditation, and the publisher cancelled seven consecutive monthly bulletins (reference months Feb-Aug 2025); the machine-readable GHIP/GB7S time series on ons.gov.uk are frozen at 2025 JAN with 'Next release: 26 March 2025'. Tiered LOW on the same grounds as its CPI sibling: symbols: [], no rates- or sterling-keyed house playbook, attribution value only. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
